rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Phenol > water > alcohol in acidity: the phenoxide ion is resonance-stabilised while the negative charge on alkoxide is trapped on oxygen — the resonance argument is the mark.  ·  Trick 2: Substituent effect: EWG (NO2) increase acidity (stabilise phenoxide); EDG (CH3) decrease — ortho/para nitrophenols are far more acidic.

rows.text: Trick 3: Kolbe: phenol → sodium phenoxide + CO2 (125 °C, 5 atm) → salicylic acid; Reimer–Tiemann: CHCl3/NaOH → salicylaldehyde — both give ORTHO products; memorise the two product types.  ·  Trick 4: Bromination: phenol + bromine water → 2,4,6-tribromophenol (white ppt) without a catalyst — the test for phenol.  ·  define + example each sub-idea: phenols, acidity, electrophilic substitution, kolbe's reaction.
